From dd39edb445f07400e748da967a07d5dca5c5f96e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Morning Star <alexbestoso@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Nov 2025 16:37:08 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: rtlwifi: 8192cu: fix tid out of range in
 rtl92cu_tx_fill_desc()

TID getting from ieee80211_get_tid() might be out of range of array size
of sta_entry->tids[], so check TID is less than MAX_TID_COUNT. Othwerwise,
UBSAN warn:

 UBSAN: array-index-out-of-bounds in drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/rtl8192cu/trx.c:514:30
 index 10 is out of range for type 'rtl_tid_data [9]'

Fixes: 8ca4cdef9329 ("wifi: rtlwifi: rtl8192cu: Fix TX aggregation")
Signed-off-by: Morning Star <alexbestoso@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ping-Ke Shih <pkshih@realtek.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/1764232628-13625-1-git-send-email-pkshih@realtek.com

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/rtl8192cu/trx.c b/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/rtl8192cu/trx.c
index aa702ba7c9f5..d6c35e8d02a5 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/rtl8192cu/trx.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/rtl8192cu/trx.c
@@ -511,7 +511,8 @@ void rtl92cu_tx_fill_desc(struct ieee80211_hw *hw,
 	if (sta) {
 		sta_entry = (struct rtl_sta_info *)sta->drv_priv;
 		tid = ieee80211_get_tid(hdr);
-		agg_state = sta_entry->tids[tid].agg.agg_state;
+		if (tid < MAX_TID_COUNT)
+			agg_state = sta_entry->tids[tid].agg.agg_state;
 		ampdu_density = sta->deflink.ht_cap.ampdu_density;
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch addresses an out-of-bounds array access in the Realtek rtl8192cu WiFi driver.

## File modifications

### `drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtlwifi/rtl8192cu/trx.c`

**Change**: In function `rtl92cu_tx_fill_desc()`, the assignment `agg_state = sta_entry->tids[tid].agg.agg_state;` is guarded by a check to ensure `tid` is less than `MAX_TID_COUNT`.

- **Before**: The `tid` value obtained from `ieee80211_get_tid(hdr)` was used directly as an index into the `sta_entry->tids[]` array without bounds checking.
- **After**: An `if (tid < MAX_TID_COUNT)` condition is added before the assignment. If the condition fails, `agg_state` remains uninitialized (presumably the function continues without aggregation state, which is benign).

This prevents a UBSAN array-index-out-of-bounds warning when a TID value >= 9 (the array size) is passed.

## Relationships

- The bug stems from the fact that `ieee80211_get_tid()` can return a value up to 15 (IEEE 802.11 TID range 0–15), but the driver’s internal `tids` array is defined with `MAX_TID_COUNT` entries (typically 9, covering TIDs 0–8). The fix ensures the array index is validated before access, avoiding undefined behavior.
- No other files are modified; the fix is self-contained within the single source file.

Root cause:
The function rtl92cu_tx_fill_desc() uses the TID value from ieee80211_get_tid() directly as an index into `sta_entry->tids[]` without checking if it is less than `MAX_TID_COUNT`. The TID can range from 0 to 15, but the array size is only 9, leading to an out-of-bounds access.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
tid = ieee80211_get_tid(hdr);
agg_state = sta_entry->tids[tid].agg.agg_state;
Reason:
The TID value obtained from `ieee80211_get_tid()` can range from 0 to 15, but `sta_entry->tids[]` has a size of `MAX_TID_COUNT` (which is 9). Using the TID directly as an array index without checking if it is less than `MAX_TID_COUNT` causes an out‑of‑bounds access, leading to the UBSAN warning.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (tid < MAX_TID_COUNT)
	agg_state = sta_entry->tids[tid].agg.agg_state;
Reason:
The fix adds a bounds check before accessing the array. If `tid` is within the valid range (0 to `MAX_TID_COUNT - 1`), the aggregation state is read; otherwise, it remains at its default value `RTL_AGG_STOP`. This prevents any out‑of‑bounds memory access.
